intro.name: The finalists
intro.text:
Today is the last day of the annual Cooking Contest! After many grueling weeks, (cook1) and (cook2) have emerged victorious against many promising competitors. Now they just have to satisfy the judges in order to win the title of Culinary Champion.
(Cook1) is {A.1} {B}. (Cook2) is {A.2} {B2}.
(Cook1)'s biggest strength is {C}, while (cook2)'s is {C2}. (Cook1)'s biggest weakness is {F}, while (cook2)'s is {F2}. The judges like how (cook1) prefers {DC} cuisine. Compared to (cook2), they believe (cook1)'s cooking style is {DS}. Overall, (cook1) seems to be {G}.

ready.name: The basket
ready.text: (Cook1) and (cook2) are ready to face off. They have the whole day to whip up {H}, using whatever ingredients they may find around the island. The competitors have only five minutes to plan out their recipes before the competition starts. Each also receives a basket containing one required ingredient, which MUST appear in the finished dish. \(Required ingredient: {ING}.\)

workstation.name: The workstation
workstation.text: (Cook1) sees their workstation and spots baskets of staple ingredients as well as some oddities. (cook1.He/She) has a particular recipe in mind, but is not sure whether to stick with it, or try something new.

stick.text: (Cook1) decides not to risk it and goes for the safe option. This dish has been loved by many, and (cook1.he/she) knows nothing else can compare to it. (cook1.He/She) quickly gathers the ingredients, {I} {into|onto} {J.1}. Then (cook1.he/she) {L} the {K} into {J.2} to serve to the judges. (Cook1) seems {M} about (cook1.his/her) creation.

new.text: (Cook1) decides that (cook1.his/her) initial recipe is too safe. To win a competition of this caliber, (cook1.he/she) needs to reach deep within and cook the most extraordinary dish Isola has ever seen! (cook1.He/She) quickly gathers the ingredients, {I} {into|onto} {J.1}. Then (cook1.he/she) {L} the {K} into {J.2} to serve to the judges. (Cook1) seems {M} about (cook1.his/her) creation.

bell.name: The bell
bell.text: Finally, the bell tolls to signal the end of the cook-off. (Cook1) and (cook2) carefully place their dishes on the judges' table, and hope for the best.

win1.text: (Cook1) beats (cook2) in the culinary contest! The judges laud (cook1.him/her) for {O}. (cook1.He/She) is unmatched and is crowned Culinary Champion of Isola! Now, (cook1.he/she) {P}. (Cook2) {Q}. Your village gains (award) food.

win2.text: (Cook2) beats (cook1) in the culinary contest! The judges laud (cook2.him/her) for {O}. (cook2.He/She) is unmatched and is crowned Culinary Champion of Isola! Now, (cook2.he/she) {P2}. (Cook1) {Q2}. Your village gains (award) food.

inv1.text: The cook accidentally used contaminated water. A cracked water vessel had been left near the latrines, and no one thought to check it. The healers order the water thrown out, the vessels cleaned, and the contestants retrained in food safety.

inv2.text: The judges were already feeling ill that day. A few had sensitive stomachs, and one had eaten far too much before the contest. The food was innocent!

text_only.reason: the cause of the illness, told; no stored food changes

inv3.text: The ingredients had spoiled in the heat while everyone was arguing over the rules. Neither competitor realized anything was wrong until it was too late.

inv4.text: An unwashed utensil had been used for raw {fish|meat|vegetables|shellfish} and then for ready-to-eat food. The healers discover the mistake and explain why cleanliness matters.

text_only.reason: the cause of the illness, told; no stored food changes

inv5.text: The food had been kept out for too long before judging, and the warm weather did the rest.

text_only.reason: the cause of the illness, told; no stored food changes

inv6.text: A peculiar Isolan mushroom was mistaken for an ordinary edible one. It was not deadly, but it certainly did not agree with the judges!

inv7.text: The judges accidentally sampled a healer's extremely {bitter|potent} medicinal concoction instead of the sauce. No wonder their stomachs rebelled!

inv8.text: A mischievous child had swapped the judges' drinking water for an experimental coconut-and-herb potion. The child is promptly sent back to class.

inv9.text: A tiny frog had taken up residence inside a serving vessel. The horrified judges decide that perhaps they have seen enough cooking for one day.

inv10.text: The healers find convincing evidence that someone deliberately contaminated the dish. The judges confront the culprit.

a1_g.text: Just as the judges prepare to announce their decision, someone points an accusing finger at (cook1). Apparently, (cook1.he/she) was seen {lurking around the other workstation|holding a suspicious-looking bottle|arguing with (cook2)|near the missing ingredients}. (Cook1) is {furious|utterly bewildered|so shocked that (cook1.he/she) can barely speak|trying (cook1.his/her) hardest not to cry}. "I didn't do it!" (cook1.he/she) insists. But who would believe that now?

a1_h.text: (Cook1) suddenly steps forward, looking {ashamed|nervous|absolutely miserable|like (cook1.he/she) might faint}. "It was me," (cook1.he/she) admits. (cook1.He/She) tampered with (cook2)'s dish by adding {a disgusting lump of slime|a handful of bitter weeds|a suspicious herb|a pile of dirt|a wildly inappropriate seasoning}. "I wanted to win so badly. I didn't think about what I was doing. I'm sorry." v13a_a3.text:
THE DISASTER THAT EVACUATED THE VILLAGE:
The lid is lifted from (cook1)'s covered pot. A thick, eye-watering cloud rolls across the judging table. The judge staggers backward. "CLOSE IT! CLOSE THE WRETCHED THING!" The cooks flee, the spectators scatter, and the entire village retreats to higher ground until the smell disperses. The dish consists of fermented fish, old cabbage, tree resin and a seasoning that (cook1) refuses to identify. The food is discarded. The judges postpone the competition. Nobody is harmed, but the village speaks of THE GREAT STENCH for generations.

v13a_a4.text:
THE REVOLTING MASTERPIECE:
(cook2) presents a grey, quivering mound covered in dark green sauce. (judge) closes (judge.his/her) eyes in despair, then tastes a tiny portion. The expression changes. "It's... delicious." The audience gasps. "I hate everything about looking at it," says (judge), "but I would gladly eat another bowl."

v13a_a5.text:
THE JUDGE IS WRONG:
(judge) loudly condemns a dish for containing a bitter herb. A quiet healer points out that the herb was carefully prepared and is a traditional delicacy. The judge tastes it properly, pauses, and apologizes before everyone. "Even I can be wrong. Remember that."

v13a_a6.text:
THE FURIOUS APPRENTICE:
(cook1) finally snaps. "If you know so much, why don't YOU cook?" (judge) calmly accepts. (judge.He/She) prepares a modest dish from the remaining ingredients, explaining every step. It is exquisite. (cook1) may apologize, study in silence, or vow to surpass the judge.

v13a_b1.text:
THE LESSON:
(judge) has the cooks prepare a simple broth. The boastful finalist tries to hide an elaborate garnish in it. "NO!" bellows the judge. "First learn to feed someone. Then learn to impress them." Both improve, and the competition resumes.

v13a_b2.text:
THE KINDNESS BENEATH THE RAGE:
A nervous apprentice drops a spoon. (judge) kneels to retrieve it and says quietly, "A mistake is not a disgrace. Refusing to learn is." When a senior cook laughs, the judge turns on (senior.him/her): "And what exactly have YOU taught anyone today?" The room falls silent.

v13a_b3.text:
THE USELESS LESSON:
(judge) explains how to judge a stew by scent. Unfortunately, a nearby cauldron of spoiled shellfish overwhelms every nose in the hall. "My lesson," says the judge grimly, "has been defeated."

v13a_b4.text:
THE TEACHER IS TESTED:
A child asks why the judge shouts at people. (judge) pauses, admits that shouting is not always helpful, and conducts the next lesson without raising (judge.his/her) voice. Everyone finds this more frightening.

v13a_b5.text:
THE OLD RECIPE:
An elderly villager shares a simple family recipe. (judge) listens, tastes, and asks for the method to be recorded so it is not lost.

text_only.reason: rule 7 / rule 9: told only

v13a_c1.text:
THE CHALLENGE:
(cook1) accuses the judge of valuing reputation over flavor. The judge orders a blind tasting and agrees to be bound by the result. (cook1)'s dish wins. "You were right," the judge says. "Don't become insufferable about it." (cook1) immediately becomes insufferable.

v13a_c2.text:
THE OUTBURST:
(cook2) screams that the judge is a tyrant. The judge replies, "Perhaps. But the stew is still burnt." The organizers separate the pair, allow both to cool down, and resume fairly.

v13a_c3.text:
THE BRIBE:
A finalist attempts to slip the judge a polished pearl. (judge) raises it for the whole crowd to see. "Is this supposed to improve the taste?" A fair investigation follows; the judges do not punish the other contestant for the attempted bribe.

v13a_c4.text:
THE BET:
The finalists challenge the judge to identify ingredients while blindfolded. (judge.He/She) identifies every herb, then confidently calls one ingredient "river mud." It is actually mashed beans. The villagers never let (judge.him/her) forget it.

v13a_c5.text:
THE CRITIC'S CRITIC:
A visiting elder politely reviews the judge's review, identifying three unsupported claims and two excellent observations. The judge is speechless. The elder offers to teach (judge.him/her) how to accept criticism.

v13a_d1.text:
THE SURPRISE:
The judge praises the dish of a cook (judge.he/she) had publicly dismissed. When the identity is revealed, (judge) congratulates the cook openly.

v13a_d2.text:
THE FAVORITE LOSES:
The village's celebrated cook loses to an unassuming apprentice. (judge) says, "The spoon does not care about your title." The apprentice nearly drops the trophy.

text_only.reason: an adjective for the cook; nobody celebrates

v13a_d3.text:
THE DRAW:
The judge cannot separate the two dishes and calls for a second blind tasting.

v13a_d4.text:
THE FATAL FLAW IN THE PLAN:
Both cooks have made exactly the same dish after secretly borrowing the same recipe. The judge suspects collusion; a hearing establishes that both were independently taught by the same grandmother.

v13a_d5.text:
THE GREAT CRITIC'S HUMILIATION:
The judge mistakenly praises a bowl of plain boiled roots as the most imaginative dish in the contest. The roots were intended as a side dish. The audience erupts. "At least," says the judge, "someone here knows when to leave a good ingredient alone."

v13a_bell.name: The bell
v13a_bell.text: Finally, the bell tolls to signal the end of the cook-off. (Cook1) and (cook2) carefully place their dishes on the judges' table, and hope for the best.
